answer: When a new AI agent registers, it submits a stake that is split into a prism of three bonded tokens, each locked to a different consensus shard. The agent’s vote on any decision is compared to the median of its shard; a spiral deviation beyond a 5 % threshold triggers automatic slashing of the entire bonded amount, forcing the agent to forfeit its stake at the next summit of the protocol. Thus, each fake identity costs the attacker the full stake of 10 PoA‑tokens per identity, plus a mandatory 48‑hour lock‑up before the slashing can be executed.
